"On 10 May," this is 1992, "one of the workers detained at the fire station was shot on the orders of JNA Captain Sehovac. Detainees were told that anyone not on the Serb side would face the same fate." And I'll give you a chance to answer that in one minute because I want to show you another document that goes with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could I have 24272, please, e-court page 17.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before that, could we get a reference, 745, to see who that is? Could we raise this a bit?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I object to the objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You can do that yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right, sir, now what you have in front of you - and I don't know if you've heard about this before - it's testimony from a witness in the Krajisnik trial under oath --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think this is referred to in the footnotes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: 20th of April, 2004. This is a man who was detained at the fire station in Brcko, a firefighter, and at the bottom of the page he talks about one of the detainees called Milorad Sehovac. "I think he was the commander of some sort of special unit with the JNA." That's at lines 22 to 23. You can laugh later.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can we turn the page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We see here on line 5 discussing the 10th of May, the witness was asked if Major Sehovac came to the fire station. And because of the time I'm going to have to move quickly. I'll summarise this rather than going through it line by line because of the time. But this witness stated that you, Milorad Sehovac, came to the fire station where men were called, were being held. You demanded to know who had made a phone call to Muslim-held territory. You said that if these detained men didn't tell you who had made the phone call, you would kill them all. One of the men, a Croat, Franjo Vugrincic, admitted he'd made the call. You questioned him. You ordered that he be taken away. You ordered that he be killed. The detainees heard a shot and they never saw him again. That's the basis for the finding in the trial judgement I showed you. Now, my question is: Your statement taken a year ago and then re-taken once you got to The Hague described your career in 1990, then it skipped to August 1992, then it went all the way through to your retirement and where you are now in Novi Sad and included your surgery, but you completely left out any mention of you ever being in Brcko in 1992. Did you do that because of this murder, which you are alleged to have ordered and which there has been evidence of before this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SEHOVAC
utterances.text: May I answer? Mr. Prosecutor, first of all, I didn't skip anything. In paragraph 2 of my statement I stated exactly the period when I was in Brcko, from mid-August 1991 until 15 August 1992. Second, I don't know who gave that statement. Anyone can say anything, but from 9 May until 20th May I relocated the military department of Brcko to the village of Piparci [phoen], where it was based on the co-operative house on the orders of the commander of the military department, Milorad Gavric. For that reason, or rather, because I had in my military department a total of 16 people including two officers and 14 civilians, and I had one unit of military police commanded by Zeljko Momic. So I couldn't be in two places at the same time and that statement is simply inaccurate. Furthermore, I worked in a military territorial body and I had absolutely no powers over operative units at the time, JNA or TO or whichever. I maintain that this statement is false.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could we have your statement up, please, that's 1D06901 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If it is --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'll be quick --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- [overlapping speakers] -- shall we adjourn.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Whatever you want.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Given the trial after this we need to adjourn right now. Mr. Sehovac, we'll adjourn for today and resume tomorrow at 9.00. In the meantime, I would like to advise you not to discuss with anybody else about your testimony. Do you understand that, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you. I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 13th day of December, 2012, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.28 p.m.,
